statement: The function returns Ok r with len(r) = n. Define d1(u,v) as the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v in the tree T1 given by edges1, and d2(u,v) similarly for T2 given by edges2. Define c1(v) = d1(0,v) mod 2 for 0 <= v < n, and c2(v) = d2(0,v) mod 2 for 0 <= v < m. Let A1 = number of v with 0 <= v < n and c1(v)=0, B1 = n - A1; A2 = number of v with 0 <= v < m and c2(v)=0, B2 = m - A2; M2 = max(A2,B2). For 0 <= i < n, let s1(i) = A1 if c1(i)=0 else B1. Then for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = s1(i) + M2.
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m <= 10^5; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: With the notation of spec_1: whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 + M2 <= r[i] <= n - 1 + M2.
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the set { r[i] : 0 <= i < n } has at most two elements.
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: Let c1(v) = (distance from 0 to v in the first tree) mod 2. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i,j with 0 <= i,j < n, if c1(i) = c1(j) then r[i] = r[j].
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: With the notation of spec_1: whenever the function returns a result r, sum_{i=0}^{n-1} r[i] = A1*A1 + B1*B1 + n*M2.

statement: With the notation of spec_1: whenever the function returns a result r, the maximum element of r is max(A1,B1) + M2, and the minimum element of r is min(A1,B1) + M2.
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: Let d1(u,v) be the distance in the first tree given by edges1, and d2(u,v) the distance in the second tree given by edges2. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, there exist x with 0 <= x < n and y with 0 <= y < m such that (number of u with 0 <= u < n and d1(i,u) even) + (number of v with 0 <= v < m and d1(i,x) + 1 + d2(y,v) even) = r[i].
preconditions: n = len(edges1)+1, m = len(edges2)+1; 2 <= n,m; each element of edges1 and edges2 has length 2; every edge of edges1 has both endpoints in [0,n) and every edge of edges2 has both endpoints in [0,m); edges1 describes a tree on nodes 0..n-1; edges2 describes a tree on nodes 0..m-1.

statement: Let d1(u,v) be the distance in the first tree given by edges1, and d2(u,v) the distance in the second tree given by edges2.
